# timeseries

Use for values over time. Line, area, bars, and overlay are display forms of this type.

Wrap the completed definition in one `notebook_cells` envelope. Do not add dashboard
layout or widget identity fields.

Cross-cutting query, formula, sort, unit, and palette rules live in
[the construction handbook](../widgets/handbook.md).

## Supported data sources

`apm_dependency_stats`, `apm_metrics`, `audit`, `ci_pipelines`, `ci_tests`, `cloud_cost`, `container`, `errors`, `events`, `incident_analytics`, `llm_observability`, `logs`, `metrics`, `network`, `on_call_events`, `process`, `product_analytics`, `product_analytics_extended`, `product_analytics_journey`, `product_analytics_retention`, `profiles`, `rum`, `security_signals`, `slo`, `spans`

## Rules and warnings

- Multiple formulas supported.
- Timeseries display types:
  - `"line"` (default): Continuous values (gauge/rate, avg|min|max|pXX). Use for trend + timing, comparing a few series. Prefer for multiple requests.
  - `"bars"`: Additive bucket totals (count/sum .as_count()). Bars fill the rollup interval so gaps are visible, not interpolated.
  - `"area"`: Stacked composition — one query grouped by a tag (e.g., by {service}). Shows part-of-whole over time. Avoid with multiple separate queries.

- Log scale axes (distribution, timeseries, heatmap): When setting `scale: "log"`, MUST also set `include_zero: false`
  (log(0) is undefined - schema doesn't document this constraint)

## Examples

- timeseries example (mixed display types, metrics):
```json
{"type":"timeseries","requests":[{"queries":[{"data_source":"metrics","name":"cpu","query":"avg:system.cpu.user{host:web-1}"}],"formulas":[{"formula":"cpu"}],"response_format":"timeseries","display_type":"line"},{"queries":[{"data_source":"metrics","name":"mem","query":"avg:system.mem.used{host:web-1}"}],"formulas":[{"formula":"mem"}],"response_format":"timeseries","display_type":"bars"}]}
```
  Note: use separate requests to mix display types (line vs bars). Each request has its own display_type. Do NOT add "legend" or "yaxis" at the widget root — use "legend_layout"/"legend_columns" if needed, or omit for defaults.
- timeseries example (spans — p50/p95 latency):
```json
{"type":"timeseries","requests":[{"queries":[{"data_source":"spans","name":"p50","search":{"query":"service:web"},"compute":{"aggregation":"pc50","metric":"@duration"},"indexes":["*"]},{"data_source":"spans","name":"p95","search":{"query":"service:web"},"compute":{"aggregation":"pc95","metric":"@duration"},"indexes":["*"]}],"formulas":[{"formula":"p50","alias":"p50"},{"formula":"p95","alias":"p95"}],"response_format":"timeseries","display_type":"line"}]}
```
  Note: spans queries use "search" (NOT "filter"), "compute" with "aggregation" and "metric", and "indexes".

## Fetch the schema

Choose the data source first, then fetch only the layer you need. Both flags
matter: `--data-source` drops the other sources' query types, and `--section`
drops the styling types. Together they are about an eighth of the full schema.

```bash
pup widgets schema timeseries --surface notebooks --data-source SOURCE --section request
```

That returns the definition, its request model, and the query and formula types.
It is what you need to write a working widget.

Fetch more only when the request calls for it:

- styling, palettes, units, axes, markers, conditional formats, cell display,
  or a widget-level timeframe: add `--section presentation`
- a visualization over an earlier analysis cell: add `--section local-dataset`

Omitted layers are listed at the end of the output with the flag that returns
them. Read that line: if a field you need is missing, it is in a layer you did
not ask for.
